card.name: Bourree
card.era: First attested as a popular dance 1665 (Clermont-Ferrand); Baroque court form mid-17th-18th c.
card.tagline: Lively French folk dance of Auvergne; also a Baroque suite movement.
card.profile: The bourree is a French dance originating in Auvergne in the Massif Central, sometimes called the 'French clog dance,' first mentioned as a popular dance in 1665 at Clermont-Ferrand (Wikipedia; Britannica). Folk forms divide into the triple-time bourree (Montagnarde - Puy-de-Dome, Haute-Loire, Cantal, Limousin) and the duple-time line bourree (Berry, Bourbonnais, Nivernais). The step glides along the ground with stamped accents and little or no physical contact between partners - connection is through the eyes - danced in couples, quadrettes, lines or circles. Traditionally accompanied by the cabrette (Auvergnat bagpipe), vielle a roue (hurdy-gurdy), and later accordion and fiddle. As a Baroque form, Bach, Handel and Chopin wrote bourrees, giving its name to the ballet step pas de bourree (Wikipedia FR; Britannica).
card.insight: The folk dance and the Baroque/court form share a name and duple-time character, but no early dance notation survives to prove a direct line between the peasant dance and the courtly concert dance (Wikipedia).
